true_blocker.conclusion: With the original lens silhouette unchanged, no interior volume can be produced by SWEEPING because the lamp components are thin shells, not solids.
measured_evidence: per-side components: 3 LEFT / 3 RIGHT (rear_lights 2, rear_lightsl 1, rear_lightsr 1, light_breake 2)
every swept candidate fails at slice 0 of the first component
measured cross-section at slice 0: 0.0 x 0.00092 m at 10 mm inset; 0.00023 x 0.01061 m at 7 mm; 0.0 x 0.0 at 5 mm; 0.0 x 0.00065 m at 3.5 mm; 0.0 x 0.00165 m at 2.5 mm
i.e. one cross-section axis is under 2 mm at every inset: the component has essentially no thickness in its own shell-normal direction
true_blocker.why_iteration_cannot_solve: the failure is not a parameter choice. The cross-section is measured FROM the component's own extent, and that extent is ~0 in one axis by construction. No combination of sweep radius, inset, cross-section or centreline can create thickness that the source surface does not have.
true_blocker.previous_approach_also_quantified: whole-cluster convex hull gave a valid closed manifold (volume 0.00130 m3, boundary 0) but goes thin BETWEEN the disjoint components, so the guide path had clearance below epsilon + 0.8 mm.
true_blocker.segmented_guide_result: not reachable yet: segmentation needs a containing volume to place segments in, and neither cavity construction produces one with usable clearance along the lamp.
true_blocker.minimum_structural_change: offset the lens SURFACE instead of sweeping a cross-section: duplicate the shell, displace it inward along its own normals by a few mm and stitch the boundary, producing a closed 'shell + inner offset' volume whose thickness is the offset. That is the only remaining construction that yields a real interior without moving the outer silhouette. It must handle the non-manifold seams in these shells, which is why it needs to be built and validated as its own pass.
